reviews.reason: The filing covers every published release of node-forge, and 1.4.0 is the newest, so no version of the pinned expo resolves without it: expo > @expo/cli > node-forge and expo > @expo/cli > @expo/code-signing-certificates > node-forge. Both callers are Node build tooling — the CLI's macOS keychain code signing and the dev code-signing certificate generator — and no module of node-forge appears in the exported Android, iOS or web bundle, so nothing this repository ships runs it. What the filing describes is a signature-verification defect (RSA PKCS#1 v1.5 verification accepting extra nested DigestAlgorithm elements) reached when the CLI reads a code-signing certificate or request, which in that flow comes from the developer's own machine rather than a remote party. Re-review when upstream releases a fixed node-forge, when the Expo CLI drops the dependency, or by this date.

The filing covers zod <4.6.6. This repository's own zod, the copy src/core/responses.ts, src/core/workspace.ts and src/packs/decide/wire.ts import, is 4.6.6, the first patched release, and both exported Hermes bundles carry only that copy: the source maps of `expo export --source-maps` list 94 of its modules in each and none from expo/node_modules/zod. 3.25.76 is the copy expo > @expo/cli resolves (^3.25.76), and it is the newest 3.x, so no release of the pinned expo resolves without it. The CLI requires it only in its development server, build/src/start/server/DevToolsPlugin.schema.js and createMCPDevToolsExtensionSchema.js, which validate the dev-tools plugin descriptors of the packages a developer installed; `expo export` does not reach them, and nothing a device or a served catalog sends is parsed there. What the filing describes is an array schema with no length bound collecting one issue per failing element until memory runs out; the CLI's arrays are the command and parameter lists inside descriptors this repository's own dependencies ship. Re-review when expo moves @expo/cli to zod 4.6.6 or later.
